children: Venrock Healthcare Capital Partners III, L.P., part of the Venrock healthcare funds, disclosed a 9.995% stake in Korsana Biosciences, Inc. common stock. The filing arrived on September 15, 2026, following Korsana’s merger closing on September 8, 2026 and name change from Cyclerion Therapeutics. The investment includes common stock, Series B preferred shares, and pre-funded warrants, with a Venrock partner already on Korsana’s board.

Venrock and affiliated funds bought the stake for investment and may buy more or sell over time. They also keep the option to push for bigger moves, including “an extraordinary corporate transaction, such as a merger, reorganization or liquidation.” Venrock partner Nimish Shah sits on the board, which gives the group direct influence on strategy.

The group faces important limits: conversion and warrant exercises cannot lift their ownership above “9.99% of the outstanding shares of common stock,” and certain holders agreed to a 180‑day lock-up after the merger. The pre-funded warrants allow cash or cashless exercise and no expiration, and the blocker can be increased with notice after a 60‑day waiting period.

Venrock is a long-running U.S. venture capital platform known for backing technology and healthcare companies, with dedicated life sciences funds like VHCP. The reporting entities are Delaware-organized investment partnerships and managers focused on venture investing in healthcare. Venrock has financed numerous biotech companies from early stages through IPOs, aiming to build value through active governance and strategic support.
